newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daiei chairman says restructuring has gone too far.
newsitem.headline: Daiei chairman says restructuring has gone too far.

text.p: Daiei Inc's chairman Isao Nakauchi said on Friday that the company has gone too far in its restructuring efforts, particularly the transfer of employees to subsidiaries.
At a news conference, Nakauchi said that the company's cost-cutting measures, such as reducing staff and increasing self-service at its stores, were not accepted by Japanese customers.
"We will call back 500 to 600 employees who are temporarily working at subsidiaries," said Nakauchi.
Nakauchi also said the company will review its plans for opening new stores. He did not elaborate further.
He also said the recent food poisoning epidemic in western Japan had a considerable impact on the company's performance in the half year ended on August 31.
"The O-157 epidemic caused our profits to decline 2.5 billion yen," Nakauchi said.
Executive vice president Jun Nakauchi told a news conference held concurrently in Tokyo that bad weather earlier this year caused sales in outdoor goods to decline.
